subject: Spatial Gradient for the latent Gaussian field through SPDE

messages.author: d7ee34c7589817da
messages.subject: Spatial Gradient for the latent Gaussian field through SPDE
parts:
HI everyone,

I am new to INLA as well as the SPDE approach for latent Gaussian field. I am currently interested in obtaining a spatial gradient/Hessian estimates of the posterior intensity field obtained from a LGCP model after using the SPDE approach.

My understanding is that there is restriction on the differentiability of the latent field given the smoothness parameter  for the Matern covariance function. Nevertheless, assume that my Matern field is differentiable (or maybe even twice differentiable) in the spatial coordinates, is there some kind of simple way of obtaining an estimates for the gradients and Hessian after getting the solution from the SPDE approach? 

My initial thought is that if the solution to the latent field is provided by a basis function expansion, it should be relatively easy to get the spatial gradient since we only need to differentiate the basis function with respect to the coordinates. But since the basis functions used in the SPDE approach is piecewise linear on the triangle mesh, won't there be locations in the field that are not differentiable? For example, points on the edge of two triangle. This seems to contradict the original assumption that the Matern field is differentiable, although my understanding here could be incorrect.

My main question here is that by using a piecewise linear function, can we simply get a gradient estimates of the latent field? If so, how should I do it in INLA? If not, will there be any development in the code to implement gradient estimates of the latent field?

Thank you very much!

Best,
David

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial Gradient for the latent Gaussian field through SPDE
parts:
The inla.spde2.matern and inla.spde.pcmatern implementations are limited to operator order alpha=2 which in dimension 2 only gives one mean square derivative of the field, so the Hessian is not well defined. The gradient of the finite element representation is piecewise constant, so it does give an approximation of the gradient at least; it's an approximation that's good for spatial integrals of the gradient (by the finite element construction) but less good for pointwise values.  The `inla.fmesher.smorg` function has a parameter `gradients` for allowing the construction of the weighting matrices dx, dy, and dz, for derivatives in different directions (For a planar mesh, dx %*% field gives x-derivatives for the whole field).

For higher order derivatives, you need a field with larger alpha value (easiest to implement via inla.rgeneric) and higher order basis functions, which is possible but not implemented in the R-INLA package.
Recall that for alpha = 2, the SPDE operator is (kappa^2 - Hessian) x(s) ds = dW(s), so the Hessian of the field is as non-continuous as spatial white noise (smoothness -1, i.e. less than continuous ), so even though one can compute an approximation in distribution sense (i.e. that has sensible properties when integrated over space, via a rescaling of the G1 matrix) the continuous interpretation doesn't have pointwise meaning.

Finn
